memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "On the same day Moses commanded the people: When you have crossed the Jordan, these tribes shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph and Benjamin." — Deut 27:11-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses arranged a dramatic ceremony for when Israel entered the land. Six tribes would stand on Mount Gerizim to pronounce blessing, and six on Mount Ebal for the curse (as the next verses describe). The people would stand in the valley between two mountains, hearing blessing on one side and curse on the other. It was a vivid, unforgettable picture of the choice set before them.

Life before God really does come down to a choice like this. There is a path of blessing that comes from walking with Him, and a path of curse that comes from turning away. God laid it out plainly so no one could claim they did not understand the stakes.

We should be careful not to read these tribal blessings as a formula for our earthly prosperity. This was covenant blessing tied to Israel's obedience under the law. But the deeper reality endures: God sets before every person a genuine choice, and it matters eternally.

Here is the wonder of the gospel. Christ stepped into the place of the curse for us. Galatians tells us He "became a curse for us" by hanging on the tree (Gal 3:13), so that the blessing might come to us who trust Him. On the cross, He took the Ebal we deserved, so we could receive the Gerizim we never earned. What amazing love.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I take seriously the choice between walking with God or away from Him?
2. How does it move me that Christ took the curse in my place?
3. Am I living in the blessing of belonging to Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You for becoming a curse for me so that I might receive blessing. Help me choose Your path each day and walk closely with You. Amen.
